narrator.instruct: Fast-paced, energetic, punchy explainer narrator. Brisk delivery with no long pauses.

coach.instruct: Overly enthusiastic gym salesman, loud, pumped up, big grin.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's January first. You just signed up for the gym, seventy dollars a month.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Best decision of your life! See you every day!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You go Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday. You feel unstoppable.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your neighbor laughs from his couch.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By March, your gym bag hasn't left the car.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the salesman rings the little bell on his desk. Your payment just went through.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The gym isn't selling you workouts. It's selling you the plan to work out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Economists tracked thousands of gym members for three years.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: New members expected to go about nine times a month. They actually went about four.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the seventy dollar plan, that's over seventeen dollars a visit.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A ten-visit pass would have cost them ten dollars a visit.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On average, they wasted about six hundred dollars.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And after their last workout, people kept paying for over two months before cancelling.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One budget chain averages around seven thousand members per gym.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That only works if they don't all show up at once.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your neighbor finally gets off the couch.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He signs up for the gym, seventy dollars a month.
